constraints: Both previous and candidate v0.6 separated chains must rebuild exactly before pairwise comparison.
An identical separated receipt and checkpoint is classified as consistent replay and not as a forward transition.
A candidate with the same ledger and anchor identity, nondecreasing self-declared epoch, later checkpoint time, all prior entries unchanged, and at least one new challenge is pairwise-admissible.
Different presented anchor ids or schemas produce a typed hold receipt.
A lower candidate self-declared anchor epoch produces a typed hold without promoting the epoch to protected monotonic state.
A different exact anchor policy digest at the same anchor identity and self-declared epoch produces a typed equivocation hold.
Reusing a checkpoint id with a different digest, presenting a different chain for the same checkpoint, time collision, or metadata-only checkpoint change produces a typed hold.
Missing or replaced prior checkpoint entries produce a typed hold with exact challenge and receipt-digest evidence.
Two synthetic candidates each pass against one prior chain, then contradict each other when co-presented; unpresented and withheld branches remain explicitly unexcluded.
Transition content and digest rebuild exactly from both full separated-chain inputs, their receipts, transition id, and caller comparison time.
A fresh Node process reloads the serialized pair, rebuilds the exact receipt, and verifies it without mutating state.
Receipts grant no host, identity, human, provider, execution, adoption, installation, promotion, merge, Foundation, or CANON authority.
Both anchor chains remain caller-presented; no Mike- or host-promoted pin was supplied.
Pairwise comparison observes only two presented chains and cannot establish consensus, total ordering, or absence of unpresented branches.
A temporary package is reloaded in a child process, but no independent receiver or retention authority is proven.
Anchor epochs and transition heads remain caller-owned and replaceable; no protected monotonic store is proven.
Ordering checks use caller timestamps; no external trusted-time receipt was supplied.
Synthetic keys and declared digests do not authenticate independent real-world controllers.
No globally consistent authority prevents two unseen branches from advancing independently.
Only synthetic chains and generated fixtures were used; no real person reviewed a current transition or plan.
No model provider or shadow experiment was invoked.
No current baseline/challenger evaluation was executed or supplied.
No voluntary held-out human outcome was observed.
